THALABI:v8p297/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p297/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p297/r4.claim: The feminine plural pronoun in خلقهن follows a broken plural for non-rational things rather than masculine-over-feminine agreement.
THALABI:v8p297/r4.anchor: إنما قال خلقهن بالتأنيث لأنه أجرى على طريق جمع التكسير

ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r11.claim: The sun and moon are created signs and ornaments of the lower heaven, so they must not be worshiped; prostration belongs to their Creator and is the most specific form of worship.
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r11.anchor: ne Şems’e ne de Kamer’e secde etmeyin çünkü onlar da sizin gibi mahluklardır

ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r12.speaker: Zemahşerî
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r12.claim: Zamakhshari says the feminine plural pronoun in khalaqahunna refers to the four signs: night, day, sun, and moon.
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r12.anchor: Zemahşerî’nin beyânına göre âyât teviliyle leyl ü nehar ve Şems ü Kamer’e râci‘olmak üzere cem‘-i müennes getirilmiştir

ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r13.claim: The pronoun may also include all the stars together with the sun and moon, as in the statements that all swim in an orbit.
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r13.anchor: Şems ü Kamer’le beraber bütün nücûma dahi ircâ‘ı melhuzdur

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p62/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p62/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p62/r6.claim: Arguments from the surrounding world reinforce God's oneness and the Hereafter, and opposition to these clear signs is condemned.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p62/r6.anchor: The argument stated in the beginning of the sūrah in favour of tawḥīd and the Hereafter is reinforced by certain other arguments found in the world around man.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p89/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p89/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p89/r1.claim: Section IV resumes the sūrah's opening arguments for God's oneness and the Hereafter from the world around us, warns those who mislead others, and identifies the Qur'an as God's revelation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p89/r1.anchor: the arguments which were presented in the beginning of the sūrah to substantiate the beliefs of tawḥīd and the Hereafter are further explained

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r3.claim: After presenting calling to God as the best speech and action, the text adduces celestial and terrestrial signs as proof of God's power, wisdom, and case.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r3.anchor: أردفه بذكر الدلائل العلوية والسفلية، وعلى قدرته الباهرة وحكمته البالغة وحجته القاطعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r4.claim: Night comes first because darkness is absence while light is existence; the sun follows the day because it illuminates the world more than the moon, whose light is said to derive from the sun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r4.anchor: قيل تنبيها على أن الظلمة عدم والنور وجود، وناسب ذكر الشمس بعد النهار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r5.claim: Some people worshipped the sun, as in the account of the Queen of Sheba and her people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r5.anchor: وكان ناس يعبدون الشمس، كما جاء في قصة بلقيس وقومها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r6.claim: He explains the feminine plural pronoun “them” as agreement with an unintelligent plural understood as feminine.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r6.anchor: لأن حكم جماعة ما لا يعقل حكم الأنثى، أي الإناث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r7.claim: He says al-Zamakhshari's explanation should distinguish small plurals from large ones; the passage coordinates four entities rather than a single plural noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r7.anchor: وكان ينبغي أن يفرق بين جمع القلة من ذلك، فإن الأفصح أن يكون كضمير الواحدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r8.claim: He also says “them” returns to the implied plural āyāt in “among His signs.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r8.anchor: ولما قال: ومن آياته، كن في معنى الآيات، فقيل: خلقهن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r9.claim: Other explanations return the pronoun to the signs just mentioned, or to sun and moon, which can be treated as a plural because of their differing cycles.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p307/r9.anchor: وقيل: يعود على الآيات المتقدم ذكرها. وقيل: على الشمس والقمر

RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r1.claim: The preceding verse commends the best deeds and calling to God; this verse follows with signs of God's existence, power, and wisdom, since calling to Him entails presenting proofs of His essence and attributes.
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r1.anchor: لما بين في الآية المتقدمة أن أحسن الأعمال والأقوا هو الدعوة إلى الله تعالى أردفه بذكر الدلائل

RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r2.claim: Night is mentioned before day because darkness is nonexistence and light is existence, and nonexistence precedes existence, hinting that these phenomena began to exist.
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r2.anchor: وإنما قدم ذكر الليل على ذكر النهار تنبيها على أن الظلمة عدم ، والنور وجود ، والعدم سابق على الوجود

RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r3.claim: Celestial bodies and other created parts of the world prove the Creator; Al-Razi points to his earlier explanations in al-Fatiha and al-Anam.
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r3.anchor: وأما دلالة الشمس والقمر والأفلاك وسائر الكواكب على وجود الصانع ، فقد شرحناها في هذا الكتاب مرارا

RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r4.claim: The sun and moon are created servants and signs of the powerful God, so prostration, the highest reverence, belongs only to the Creator.
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r4.anchor: والسجدة عبارة عن نهاية التعظيم فهي لا تليق إلا بمن كان أشرف الموجودات

RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r5.claim: Some people, including star-worshipping Sabians, claimed prostrating to the sun and moon was a means of prostrating to God; the verse forbids that intermediary and directs worship only to the Maker.
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r5.anchor: كالصابئين في عبادتهم الكواكب ويزعمون أنهم يقصدون بالسجود لهما السجود لله

RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r6.claim: Al-Razi assigns the feminine plural pronoun to night, day, and moon; nonrational plural nouns take feminine agreement, and من آياته is also treated as feminine.
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r6.anchor: والضمير في قوله { خلقهن } لليل والنهار والقمر ، لأن حكم جماعة ما لا يعقل حكم الأنثى

RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r7.claim: Although one might propose the sun as a prayer direction, habitual prostration toward its exalted, luminous body could make people think the sun is worshipped.
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r7.anchor: فلو أذن الشرع في جعلها قبلة في الصلوات ، فعند اعتياد السجود إلى جانب الشمس ربما غلب على الأوهام

RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r8.claim: A stone can serve as a qibla without suggesting divinity, so the intended benefit of orientation remains while the risk associated with the sun disappears.
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r8.anchor: بخلاف الحجر المعني فإنه ليس فيه ما يوهم الإلهية ، فكان المقصود من القبلة حاصلا

RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r9.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r9.claim: Al-Shafii locates the prostration verse at تعبدون because واسجدوا لله connects to it.
RAZI-FULL:v27p111/r9.anchor: مذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه أن موضع السجود هو قوله { تعبدون } لأجل أن قوله

STUDYQURAN:41:37/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:37/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:41:37/r1.claim: The verse joins the night, day, sun, and moon among God’s signs, as in other passages on their movement and subservience.
STUDYQURAN:41:37/r1.anchor: and that He made the sun and the moon subservient (cf. 16:12; 35:13; 39:5)

STUDYQURAN:41:37/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:37/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:41:37/r2.claim: Outwardly, the verse clearly commands worship through prostration to God alone.
STUDYQURAN:41:37/r2.anchor: Outwardly, the command to prostrate only to God is clear

STUDYQURAN:41:37/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:37/r3.speaker: Aj, Q
STUDYQURAN:41:37/r3.claim: An inward reading treats the command as overcoming the lower self, which turns toward worldly distractions instead of remembering God.
STUDYQURAN:41:37/r3.anchor: which turns toward all kinds of worldly distractions at the expense of remembering God (Aj, Q)

TAB-FULL:v20p436/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p436/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p436/r1.claim: The alternation of night and day and the sun and moon are signs proving God’s oneness and immense sovereignty; the sun does not overtake the moon, and each moves in its orbit.
TAB-FULL:v20p436/r1.anchor: لا الشمس تدرك القمر {ولا الليل سابق النهار وكل في فلك يسبحون} [يس: 40]

TAB-FULL:v20p436/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p436/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p436/r2.claim: The luminaries move only by God’s direction and cannot independently benefit or harm; worship belongs to God, who could remove their light and leave people lost in darkness.
TAB-FULL:v20p436/r2.anchor: لا بأنهما يقدران بأنفسهما على سير وجري دون إجراء الله إياهما

TAB-FULL:v20p436/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p436/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p436/r3.claim: The feminine plural pronoun refers to the four things named—night, day, sun, and moon; Arabic commonly uses feminine agreement for nonhuman plurals.
TAB-FULL:v20p436/r3.anchor: لأن من شأنهم أن يؤنثوا أخبار الذكور من غير بني آدم في الجمع

TAB-FULL:v20p437/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p437/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p437/r1.claim: Worshipping God means humbling oneself in obedience and dedicating worship to Him alone, without associating anything with Him.
TAB-FULL:v20p437/r1.anchor: يقول: إن كنتم تعبدون الله، وتذلون له بالطاعة؛ وإن من طاعته أن تخلصوا له العبادة، ولا تشركوا في طاعتكم إياه

BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r1.claim: ‘Among His signs’ means signs of God’s power.

BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r2.speaker: الإمام المرزوقي
BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r2.claim: Al-Marzūqī pairs night with day and the night with the daytime period.
BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r2.anchor: قال الإمام المرزوقي : الليل بإزاء النهار

BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r3.claim: The sun accompanies daytime and the moon nighttime; both are creatures subjected to God’s command.

BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r4.claim: Their alternation and subjection serve creatures’ needs and plainly demonstrate God’s existence, oneness, knowledge, and wisdom.
BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r4.anchor: تعاقب الليل والنهار على الوجه الذي يتفرع عليه منافع الخلق ومصالحهم وتذلل الشمس والقمر لما يراد منهما من أظهر العلامات الدالة على وجوده تعالى ووحدانيته

BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r5.claim: The signs invite the seeker to look now with the heart’s eye at God’s workmanship, including the revival of the earth and the lengthening of the shade, in hope of seeing Him by His grace in the hereafter.
BURSEVI:v8p202#2/r5.anchor: امروز از صنع من بامن نكر بديده دل

BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r1.claim: Do not prostrate to the sun or moon because they are created beings subjected to commands just as humans are.
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r1.anchor: لأنهما من جملة مخلوقاته المسخرة لأوامره مثلكم

BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r2.speaker: أهل الظاهر
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r2.claim: For outward interpreters, the command is creational rather than a legal command, since the sun and moon lack knowledge and choice.
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r2.anchor: والمراد : الأمر التكويني لا التكليفي إذ لا علم لهما ولا اختيار عند أهل الظاهر

BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r3.speaker: أهل الحقيقة
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r3.claim: For the people of spiritual reality the matter is otherwise: all creation is obedient, so fairness requires the human seeker to obey as well, as Saʿdī’s verse says.
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r3.anchor: وأما عند أهل الحقيقة ، فالأمر بخلافه.

BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r4.claim: هن refers to the four signs; the non-rational plural takes a feminine singular pronoun, or the pronoun may refer to the feminine noun ‘signs’.
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r4.anchor: الضمير للأربعة ؛ لأن حكم جماعة ما لا يعقل حكم الأنثى

BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r5.claim: Calling all four signs created things, even though the sun and moon alone suffice as examples, emphasizes their complete dependence and their inability to merit worship.
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r5.anchor: وتعليق الفعل بالكل مع كفاية بيان مخلوقية الشمس والقمر للإيذان بكمال سقوطهما عن رتبة المسجودية

BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r6.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r6.claim: The Mathnawī says the sun is God’s servant that cooks for people, so calling it God is foolish; it cannot remedy its own darkness or serve as a refuge when it disappears at night.
BURSEVI:v8p202#3/r6.anchor: وفي المثنوي : آفتاب ازامر حق طباخ ماست ابلهى باشدكه كوييم او خداست

BURSEVI:v8p203/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p203/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p203/r1.claim: If they worship God alone, they must not prostrate to anyone else; prostration is the highest form of worship and belongs exclusively to Him.
BURSEVI:v8p203/r1.anchor: إن كنتم تعبدون إياه لا تسجدوا لغيره

BURSEVI:v8p203/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p203/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p203/r2.claim: Some may have worshipped the sun and moon like the star-worshipping Sabians while claiming to intend worship through them; the verse forbids this mediation and commands worship of their Creator alone.
BURSEVI:v8p203/r2.anchor: كالصابئين في عبادتهم الكواكب ويزعمون أنهم يقصدون بالسجود لهما السجود

BURSEVI:v8p203/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p203/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p203/r3.claim: The sun cannot be made the prayer direction because its radiance, stature, and benefits could make some people mistake prostration toward it for worship of it; a designated stone direction is less suggestive of divinity.

BURSEVI:v8p203/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p203/r4.speaker: عكرمة
BURSEVI:v8p203/r4.claim: ʿIkrima reports that at sunset the sun enters a sea beneath the Throne, glorifies God, and asks not to rise because people worship it; God tells it to rise, and Hell is led against the idolaters by thirteen thousand angels.
BURSEVI:v8p203/r4.anchor: وعن عكرمة قال : إن الشمس إذا غربت دخلت بحرا تحت العرش

BURSEVI:v8p203/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p203/r5.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v8p203/r5.claim: A hadith says faith in the Prophet’s community is firm even if deeds are shown off, and that placing one’s forehead in prostration to God frees a person from pride; Bursevī gives no grading.
BURSEVI:v8p203/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث : "ليس في أمتي رياء إن راءوا فبالأعمال

TABATABAI:41:36-37/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:36-37/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:36-37/r10.claim: After affirming the call’s goodness and directing the Prophet to answer well, the passage returns to the original invitation and argues for divine unity and resurrection through three signs.
TABATABAI:41:36-37/r10.anchor: لما ذكر سبحانه كون دعوته صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أحسن القول ووصاه أن يدفع بأحسن الخصال عاد إلى أصل الدعوة

TABATABAI:41:36-37/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:36-37/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:36-37/r11.claim: The night, day, sun, and moon show one governing order, hence one Lord; that unity entails worshipping Him alone.
TABATABAI:41:36-37/r11.anchor: وحدة التدبير واتصاله على وحدة الرب المدبر

TABATABAI:41:36-37/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:36-37/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:36-37/r12.claim: The prohibition answers the implied question of what to do: the sun and moon are created and governed, so worship and prostrate only to their Creator.
TABATABAI:41:36-37/r12.anchor: فقيل لا تسجدوا للشمس ولا للقمر هما مخلوقان

TABATABAI:41:36-37/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:36-37/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:36-37/r13.claim: Polytheists generally venerated the sun and moon, though it is said that only the Sabeans worshipped them.
TABATABAI:41:36-37/r13.anchor: وعامة الوثنيين كانوا يعظمون الشمس والقمر وإن لم يعبدهما غير الصابئين على ما قيل

TABATABAI:41:36-37/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:36-37/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:36-37/r14.claim: The feminine plural pronoun refers to the night, day, sun, and moon.

TABATABAI:41:36-37/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:36-37/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:36-37/r15.claim: Worship of God is incompatible with worship of anyone else.
TABATABAI:41:36-37/r15.anchor: أي إن عبادته لا تجامع عبادة غيره

TABRISI:41:36-39/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:36-39/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:36-39/r9.claim: These are proofs of God's oneness and signs of attributes by which He differs from all creatures.
TABRISI:41:36-39/r9.anchor: أي حججه الدالة على وحدانيته وأدلته على صفاته التي باين بها جميع خلقه

TABRISI:41:36-39/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:36-39/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:36-39/r10.claim: Night is the sun's departure from the earth's surface, and day its rising over it; both follow stable measures and an enduring order.
TABRISI:41:36-39/r10.anchor: { الليل } بذهاب الشمس عن بسيط الأرض { والنهار } بطلوعها على وجهها

TABRISI:41:36-39/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:36-39/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:36-39/r11.claim: The sun and moon have distinctive lights and display ordered motion in their courses.
TABRISI:41:36-39/r11.anchor: وما اختصا به من النور وظهر فيهما من التدبير في المسير

TABRISI:41:36-39/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:36-39/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:36-39/r12.claim: Despite their many benefits, the sun and moon are not creators and must not be worshipped.
TABRISI:41:36-39/r12.anchor: وإن كان فيهما منافع كثيرة لأنهما ليسا بخالقين

TABRISI:41:36-39/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:36-39/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:36-39/r13.claim: The feminine plural pronoun can refer to a nonrational plural, which may take feminine singular or plural agreement, as in his example about sheep.
TABRISI:41:36-39/r13.anchor: أن ضمير غير ما يعقل على لفظ التأنيث تقول هذا كباشك فسقها وإن شئت قلت فسقهن

TABRISI:41:36-39/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:36-39/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:36-39/r14.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to the meaning of آيات, since the verse introduces these objects as God's signs.
TABRISI:41:36-39/r14.anchor: والآخر: أن الضمير يرجع إلى معنى الآيات لأنه قال ومن آياته

TABRISI:41:36-39/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:36-39/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:36-39/r15.claim: If they truly intend to worship God, they must prostrate to Him alone and no other.
TABRISI:41:36-39/r15.anchor: إن كنتم تقصدون بعبادتكم الله كما تزعمون الله فاسجدوا لله دون غيره

TABRISI:41:36-39/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:36-39/r19.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسن
TABRISI:41:36-39/r19.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and al-Ḥasan place the prostration-of-recitation after إن كنتم إياه تعبدون; Abū ʿAmr chooses this placement, also reported from the Imams.
TABRISI:41:36-39/r19.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود والحسن أنه عند قوله { إن كنتم إياه تعبدون } وهو اختيار أبي عمرو

QASHANI:41:36-39/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:41:36-39/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:41:36-39/r4.claim: Night is the self's darkness veiling the light and making one prone to sins and satanic whispers; day is the spirit's light shining from the heart, enabling good deeds, resistance to evil, and receptivity to divine breezes.
QASHANI:41:36-39/r4.anchor: ليل ظلمة النفس بظهور صفاتها الساترة للنور لتقعوا في السيئات وتستعدوا لقبول الوساوس الشيطانية ونهار نور الروح بإشراق أشعتها من القلب إلى النفس

QASHANI:41:36-39/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:41:36-39/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:41:36-39/r5.claim: The sun is the spirit; one must not annihilate in it and stop there, becoming veiled from the Real.
QASHANI:41:36-39/r5.anchor: بالفناء فيه والوقوف معه والاحتجاب به عن الحق

QASHANI:41:36-39/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:41:36-39/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:41:36-39/r6.claim: The moon is the heart; one must not stop with its virtues and perfections or incline to the Paradise of attributes.
QASHANI:41:36-39/r6.anchor: بالوقوف مع الفضائل والكمالات والنبو إلى جنة الصفات

QASHANI:41:36-39/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:41:36-39/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:41:36-39/r7.claim: True prostration is annihilation in the divine essence, reserving worship for God alone in un veiled unity.
QASHANI:41:36-39/r7.anchor: { واسجدوا لله الذي خلقهن } بالفناء في الذات { إن كنتم } موحدين، مخصصين العبودية به دون غيره لا مشركين ولا محجوبين

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r1.speaker: Zemahşerî, Râzî, İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r1.claim: Some commentators take the verse's addressees to be the Sabaeans, but the author rejects limiting the audience to them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r1.anchor: meselâ bk. Zemahşerî, III, 392; Râzî, XXVII, 129; İbn Âşûr, 299-300

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r2.claim: Archaeology indicates a pre-Islamic South Arabian triad of moon, sun, and Venus worship; related celestial cults spread into the Hijaz, so paganism there also informs the verse's audience.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r2.anchor: arkeolojik kaynaklar, İslâm’dan önce Güney Arabistan’da ay, güneş ve Zühre (Aster, Işter) yıldızlarından oluşan üçlü bir tanrı sistemine inanıldığını göstermektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r3.claim: Pre-Islamic Arab solar worship extended back to before the Common Era; Lāt and ʿUzzā, named with Manāt in the Qur'an, were regarded as sun goddesses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r3.anchor: Kur’an’da Menât’la birlikte anılan (Necm 53/19) Lât ve Uzzâ, güneşi temsil eden birer tanrıça sayılıyorlardı.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r4.claim: Wadd was a prominent South Arabian moon god; his name appears in North Arabian inscriptions and among Qur'anic gods of the Age of Ignorance.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r4.anchor: Kur’an’da Câhiliye tanrıları arasında Ved ismi de geçmektedir (Nûh 71/23).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r5.claim: Personal names meaning servant of Wadd or servant of the sun further show that lunar and solar worship was widespread in North Arabia and the Hijaz.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r5.anchor: Abdüved (Ved’in kulu), Abdüşşems (güneşin kulu) gibi erkek isimlerinin kullanılması, aya ve güneşe tapınmanın Kuzey Arabistan ve Hicaz’da da yaygın olduğunu gösteren başka kanıtlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r6.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says he could not establish that Arabs at the Qur'an's time worshipped the sun and moon; the author says this should not be taken as proof such worship was absent.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r6.anchor: İbn Âşûr’un, “Kur’an’ın indiği dönemde Araplar arasında güneşe ve aya tapanların bulunduğunu tesbit edemedim” şeklindeki ifadesini (XXIV, 299), doğrudan doğruya bu gök cisimlerine tapınmanın bulunmadığı anlamında düşünmek gerekir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r7.claim: The night and day cycle and the sun and moon are signs and proofs of divine power; reason therefore points to worshipping their Creator rather than them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r7.anchor: Âyette, gece ve gündüzün akışı gibi güneş ve ayın varlığı da ilâhî kudretin birer işareti, kanıtı olduğuna göre bu tür gök cisimlerine tapmak yerine onları yaratan Allah’a tapmanın gerekli olduğu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r8.claim: Only the exalted Creator deserves worship; all things and phenomena besides God are created and thus unworthy of worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:37/r8.anchor: tapılmaya lâyık olanın, sadece yüce yaratıcı olduğu, O’nun dışındaki bütün nesneler, olgular yaratılmış olduklarından bunların tapılmaya da değer olmadıkları gerçeğidir

BURHAN:v4p93#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p93#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p93#2/r1.claim: When the same definite noun is repeated, the second usually refers to the first; examples include hardship in 94:5–6, the path in the Fatiha, and celestial objects in 41:37.
BURHAN:v4p93#2/r1.anchor: فالأول إن يكونا معرفتين والثاني فيه هو الأول غالبا

QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r1.claim: The alternation of night and day and the courses of sun and moon are signs of God’s power and proofs of His oneness.
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r1.anchor: واختلاف الليل والنهار ، ودوران الشمس والقمر من جملة أمارات قدرته ، ودلالات توحيده

QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r2.claim: The sun’s height and the moon’s brightness are no grounds for worship; God is jealous for the servant’s devotion and commands prostration to their Creator.
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r2.anchor: في علائها ، { ولا للقمر } في ضيائه ، { واسجدوا لله } فقد غار عليك أن تسجد لغيره

QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r3.claim: Although sun and moon are lofty and beautiful, they were created for human benefit, so people should worship their Creator rather than them.
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r3.anchor: والشمس - وإن علت ، والقمر - وإن حسن . . . فلأجلك خلقناهما ، فلا تسجد لهما ، واسجد لنا

QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r4.claim: God commanded the angels, despite their abundant worship and precedence in obedience, to bow to Adam; by contrast, He tells sinful human descendants not to bow to sun and moon.
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r4.anchor: خلق الملائكة - ومع كثرة عبادتهم ، ومع تقدمهم في الطاعة - قال لهم : اسجدوا لآدم

QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r5.claim: The command to protect one’s face from sun and moon exposes the indignity of moving one’s feet for every base desire and presenting oneself before everyone.
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r5.anchor: والحق - سبحانه وتعالى - يأمرك بصيانة وجهك عن الشمس والقمر

BURHAN:v2p131/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p131/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p131/r10.claim: Rising stars attract idolaters by their splendor; the sun's setting is retreat, and it rises and sets between Satan's horns, while revelation forbids its worship.
BURHAN:v2p131/r10.anchor: وطلوع الكواكب نحو المشرق ومن هناك إقبالها وذلك أشرف لها وأكبر لشأنها عند المفتونين

BURHAN:v2p131/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p131/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p131/r11.claim: Repentance remains open until the sun rises from the East; the people exposed to it are captivated, though worship of sun and moon is forbidden.
BURHAN:v2p131/r11.anchor: ولأجل ما بين معنى الإقبال والإدبار كان باب التوبة مفتوحا من جهته إلى يوم تطلع الشمس منه

BURHAN:v3p233/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p233/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p233/r4.claim: Putting إياه before تعبدون preserves the cadence and sound pattern of the verse endings.
BURHAN:v3p233/r4.anchor: الثالث أن يكون في التأخير إخلال بالتناسب فيقدم 4 لمشاكلة الكلام

BURHAN:v3p366/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p366/r5.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v3p366/r5.claim: One explanation takes the feminine plural pronoun in خلقهن back to the signs just mentioned: night, day, sun, and moon.
BURHAN:v3p366/r5.anchor: فقيل الضمير عائد على الآيات المتقدمة في اللفظ

BURHAN:v3p366/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p366/r6.speaker: البغوي
BURHAN:v3p366/r6.claim: Al-Baghawi says خلقهن uses feminine agreement with a broken plural of non-rational things rather than masculine-over-feminine agreement.
BURHAN:v3p366/r6.anchor: وقال البغوى إنما قال ﴿ خلقهن ﴾ بالتأنيث لأنه أجرى على طريق جمع التكسير

SULAMI:v2p220/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p220/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p220/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says signs are shown so people seek their Manifestor; attending to the signs distracts from Him, while attending to Him prevents other distractions.
SULAMI:v2p220/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : اظهر لك الآيات لتشتغل بمظهرها دونها فمن اشتغل بها شغلته عن مظهرها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r1.claim: A singular “moon” is not genuinely indefinite, since there is only one moon; “crescent” can be indefinite more fully because multiple crescents exist.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r1.anchor: ليس المنكر غير المعرف على أن للهلال في هذا التنكير فضل تمكن ليس للقمر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r2.claim: The Qur’an uses the plural for crescents but not moon, illustrating the difference between the forms.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r2.anchor: ولم يجمع القمر على هذا الحد

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r3.claim: Al-Buhturi provides what Jurjani calls a subtle example of indefinite wording with his phrase “two moons.”
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r3.anchor: ومن لطيف هذا التنكير قول البحتري

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r4.claim: Jurjani finds Abu Tammam’s moon image awkward because it suggests multiple moons that are both far away and near in brightness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r4.anchor: يتظلم منه المعنى وينكره قول أبي تمام

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r5.claim: The sense works better with a definite moon, as in al-Buhturi’s line: despite its great height, its light is close to night travelers.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r5.anchor: فالذي يستقيم عليه الكلام أن يؤتى به معرفا على حده في بيت البحتري

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r6.claim: One can force a new sentence after “a moon,” but the phrasing still sits badly with the intended meaning.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r6.anchor: فإن قلت أقطع واستأنف فأقول كأنه هلال وأسكت

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r7.speaker: سعيد بن حميد
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r7.claim: Saʿid b. Humayd’s poem says he arranged a visit at night because that is the customary time for the moon to rise.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r7.anchor: في هذا الفن ويجب أن يوازن بينه وبين ما مضى قول سعيد بن حميد

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r8.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r8.claim: Asked why he prefers night over bright day, the speaker answers that he does not want to change the established custom of moonrise.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r8.anchor: قال لي لا احب تغيير رسمي هكذا الرسم في طلوع البدور

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r9.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r9.claim: Jurjani gives an opposing dawn version: the beloved comes in the morning because she is the sun, which rises then.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p271/r9.anchor: قلت زوري فأرسلت أنا آتيك سحره

MAJAZ:v2p197/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p197/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p197/r1.claim: The feminine plural pronoun refers to night, day, sun, and moon; after mentioning the sun and moon as objects of worship, the verse redirects worship to their Creator. Mixed or collective groups are expressed in the feminine.
MAJAZ:v2p197/r1.anchor: أي خلق الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر فلما انتهى الكلام إلى الشمس والقمر وهما يعبدان نهى عن عبادتهما

SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari lets the feminine plural pronoun refer to all four coordinated objects because nonrational plurals may take feminine agreement; the Sheikh says he fails to distinguish plurals of paucity from abundance.
SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r1.anchor: وفي مجيء الضمير كضمير الإناث - كما قال الزمخشري - هو أن جمع ما لا يعقل

SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r2.claim: The Sheikh says nonrational plurals of paucity most properly take feminine plural agreement, while plurals of abundance take feminine singular; these four separate coordinated nouns function like one plural expression.
SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r2.anchor: وناقشه الشيخ من حيث إنه لم يفرق بين جمع القلة والكثرة في ذلك؛ لأن الأفصح في جمع القلة

SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r3.claim: The author replies that al-Zamakhshari explains why feminine agreement occurs despite three masculine and one feminine antecedents: masculine normally prevails, or the referent is the feminine plural آيات.
SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r3.anchor: قلت: والزمخشري ليس في مقام بيان الفصيح والأفصح، بل في مقام كيفية مجيء الضمير ضمير إناث

SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows the pronoun to refer to the implied feminine plural آيات in ومن آياته.
SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r4.anchor: أو لما قال: " ومن آياته " كن في معنى الآيات فقيل: خلقهن، ذكره الزمخشري أيضا

SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r5.claim: A third referent is the sun and moon: the dual is treated as a plural, and Arabic has the plurals شموس and أقمار.
SAMIN-DURR:41:37/r5.anchor: الثالث: أنه يعود على الشمس والقمر؛ لأن الاثنين جمع، والجمع مؤنث، ولقولهم: شموس وأقمار.

ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r1.claim: The night, day, sun, and moon are signs that show God is one.
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r1.anchor: أي من علاماته التي تدل على أنه واحد

ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r2.claim: The feminine pronoun may refer to non-rational plurals, which take feminine agreement; a masculine plural pronoun is reserved for rational beings.
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r2.anchor: أحدهما أن ضمير غير ما يعقل على لفظ

ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r3.claim: Alternatively, the feminine pronoun refers to the implied feminine plural āyāt, since the listed objects are called God's signs.
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون (خلقهن) راجعا على معنى الآيات

ASAD-NOTES:41:37#n33/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:41:37#n33/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:41:37#n33/r1.claim: Razi connects this prohibition and call to worship God with the earlier phrase about calling people unto God in 41:33.
ASAD-NOTES:41:37#n33/r1.anchor: This, according to Razi, connects with the phrase "calling (one's fellow-men] unto God" in verse 33 above.

ASAD-NOTES:41:37#n33/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:41:37#n33/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:41:37#n33/r2.claim: In this context, adoration means ascribing real power to something.
ASAD-NOTES:41:37#n33/r2.anchor: to ascribe real power (which is the meaning of "adoration" in this context) to anything created

ASAD-NOTES:41:37#n33/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:41:37#n33/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:41:37#n33/r3.claim: God alone is the cause and source of existence; created phenomena are signs of His power, so attributing real power to any created phenomenon, force, circumstance, or idea is unreasonable and blasphemous.
ASAD-NOTES:41:37#n33/r3.anchor: God is the sole cause and source of all that exists; and whatever exists is but a wondrous sign of His creative power.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p90/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p90/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p90/r1.claim: Verse 37 returns to the creation arguments in 41:9–12; intervening warnings, reminders, and assurances leave the discourse coherent.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p90/r1.anchor: In verses 9 to 12 of this sūr ah arguments are drawn from the creation of the heavens and the earth on the doctrines of monotheism and the Hereafter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p90/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p90/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p90/r2.claim: The night, day, sun, and moon are signs of their Creator; their cycles, rising, and setting show they are subordinate, not gods or partners.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p90/r2.anchor: Their alternation and rising and setting bear witness to their subservience. From their very existence, they bear evidence that they are neither God nor His partners in any way

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p90/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p90/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p90/r3.claim: God fitted these celestial bodies into the universe's machinery to perform their assigned service at His command.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p90/r3.anchor: the Almighty has fitted them as spare-parts in the machinery of this universe, and at His bidding are

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r1.claim: They carry out their assigned service; they are signs of God's power, wisdom, mercy, and providence, and only a few among many such signs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r1.anchor: discharging the service assigned to them. After this testimony of theirs, it is mere foolishness and ignorance to regard them God or His partners.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r2.claim: Worshipping these created signs belittles both God and the worshippers; only their Creator is worthy of worship and made them serve humanity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r2.anchor: those who worship them not only belittle God but also their own selves.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r3.claim: Prostration here stands for worship because it is worship's most prominent outward manifestation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r3.anchor: The word prostration here connotes worship because it is the most prominent manifestation of worship.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r4.claim: The prohibition singles out sun and moon worship because idolatrous peoples have worshipped them in every age.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r4.anchor: It is specially stressed that people should not worship the sun and the moon because idolatrous nations have worshipped them in every age.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r5.claim: The pronoun in “created them” refers to all the objects just mentioned.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r5.anchor: refers to all the objects mentioned earlier.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r6.claim: Pure worship of God requires prostrating to no one besides Him; prostration is worship's greatest manifestation and belongs to God alone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r6.anchor: one can only fulfil the right of purely worshipping God if none except Him is prostrated to.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r7.speaker: idolaters of Arabia
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r7.claim: They worshipped other beings believing them to be means of gaining God's favour, and viewed that worship as equivalent to worshipping God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r7.anchor: the idolaters of Arabia worshipped other things besides God, it was because they thought that these things are a means

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r8.claim: The wording refutes that rationale: worship belongs to God alone, with no one sharing its distinctive acts.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p91/r8.anchor: These words refute this claim: God should be worshipped alone such that no one should even share the specific signs of this worship with anyone.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r1.claim: Night and day are signs in their origination, alternation, and each entering into the other.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r1.anchor: في حدوثهما وتعاقبهما وإيلاج كل منهما في الآخر

ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r2.claim: The sun and moon are signs in their illumination and differences of light, size, and motions.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r2.anchor: في استنارتهما واختلافهما في قوة النور والعظم والحركات مثلا

ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r3.claim: One explanation for mentioning night first is to signal its precedence, even though darkness is nonexistence.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r3.anchor: وقدم ذكر الليل قيل : تنبيها على تقدمه مع كون الظلمة عدما

ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r4.claim: The sun follows day because it is day’s sign and cause of its illumination, and because the moon’s light is said to derive from sunlight.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r4.anchor: وناسب ذكر الشمس بعد النهار لأنها آيته وسبب تنويره ولأنها أصل لنور القمر بناء على ما قالوا من أنه مستفاد من ضياء الشمس

ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r5.claim: The common view is that the sun’s light is not borrowed from another body; some attribute it to the Throne, while contemporary philosophers suspect another body and claim a small dark spot at the sun’s edge.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r5.anchor: وأما ضياؤها فالمشهور أنه غير طاريء عليها من جرم آخر وقيل : هو من العرش والفلاسفة اليوم يظنون أنه من جرم آخر

ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r6.claim: Do not worship the sun or moon because they are created things subjected to God’s will, like the worshippers themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r6.anchor: لأنها من جملة مخلوقاته سبحانه وتعالى المسخرة علة وفق إرادته تعالى مثلكم

ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r7.claim: One view makes the pronoun refer to all four signs; the sun and moon are primary objects of the command, while including night and day signals their lack of knowledge and choice.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r7.anchor: الضمير قيل للأربعة المذكورة والمقصود تعليق الفعل بالشمس والقمر لكن نظم معهما الليل والنهار إشعارا بأنهما من عداد ما لا يعلم ولا يختار

ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says a nonrational plural takes feminine agreement, as in the examples about cutting the logs; this removes the need to explain the form by treating the signs as feminine.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r8.anchor: وحكم جماعة ما لا يعقل على ما قال الزمخشري حكم الأنثى فيقال : الأقلام بريتها وبريتهن

ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r9.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r9.claim: Abu Hayyan distinguishes small-number plurals, usually paired with singular feminine agreement, from abundance plurals, more eloquently paired with feminine plural agreement; he notes this form is not literally a small-number plural.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r9.anchor: نعم قال أبو حيان : ينبغي أن يفرق بين جمع القلة من ذلك وجمع الكثرة فإن الأفصح في الأول أن يكون بضمير الواحدة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r10.claim: Other proposals limit the pronoun to the sun and moon, whose collective forms are nonrational plurals, or make it refer to the signs previously mentioned.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#2/r10.anchor: وقيل : الضمير للشمس والقمر والإئتان جمع وجمع ما لا يعقل يؤنث

ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#3/r1.claim: Prostration is the highest degree of worship, so it must be reserved for God alone.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#3/r1.anchor: فإن السجود أقصى مراتب العبادة فلا بد من تخصيصه به عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#3/r2.speaker: علي وابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#3/r2.claim: Ali and Ibn Masud used to prostrate at the end of this verse, at taʿbudūn.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#3/r2.anchor: وكان علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وابن مسعود يسجدان عند ( تعبدون )

ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#3/r3.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#3/r3.claim: The view that the prostration point is taʿbudūn is attributed to al-Shafiʿi.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#3/r3.anchor: ونسب القول بأنه موضع السجدة للشافعي

ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#3/r7.claim: Some explain the later prostration point as precaution: delay is allowed if the earlier point is intended, but advancing it is not allowed if the later point is intended.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p125#3/r7.anchor: وعلله بعضهم بالإحتياط لأنها إن كانت عند ( تعبدون ) جاز التأخير لقصر الفصل وإن كانت عند ( يسأمون ) لم يجز تعجيلها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p175#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p175#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p175#2/r2.claim: Night, day, sun, and moon are signs of God's power; worship God alone rather than prostrating to the sun or moon.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p175#2/r2.anchor: ومن آياته الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر لا تسجدوا للشمس ولا للقمر واسجدوا لله الذي خلقهن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p175#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p175#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p175#2/r3.claim: The feminine plural pronoun khalaqahunna follows the broken-plural construction and does not use masculine predominance over feminine nouns.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p175#2/r3.anchor: بالتأنيث لأنه أجراها على طريق جمع التكسير

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r5.claim: Night, day, sun, and moon are signs of God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r5.anchor: ومن ءايته اليل والنهار والشمس والقمر

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r6.claim: They are creatures subject to command, just as humans are, so they are not to be worshipped.

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r7.claim: The pronoun refers to all four preceding signs; mentioning them together suggests that they belong among things without knowledge or choice.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r7.anchor: الضمير للأربعة المذكورة، والمقصود تعليق الفعل بهما إشعارا بأنهما من عداد ما لا يعلم ولا يختار

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r8.claim: Worship God who created them; prostration is the most specific form of worship.

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r9.claim: The author places the prostration of recitation at this verse because it contains the command; Abu Hanifa places it at the end of the following verse, where the meaning is complete.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:36-37/r9.anchor: وهو موضع السجود عندنا لاقتران الأمر به، وعند أبي حنيفة آخر الآية الأخرى لأنه تمام المعنى

BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r2.claim: After describing the polytheists' idols and the virtue of prayer, the author presents cosmic signs as proofs of monotheism that dispel all rivals and illuminate God's essence and attributes through His acts.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r2.anchor: أتبعه دلائل التوحيد إعلاما بأن التوحيد أحسن الحسن يطرد كل شيء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r3.claim: Night and day, sun and moon are signs of God's oneness; their arrangement demonstrates power over resurrection and every possible thing.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r3.anchor: أي الدالان باختلافهما وهيئتهما على قدرته على البعث وعلى كل مقدور

BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r4.claim: Night precedes day because darkness is nonexistence and light is existence; the sun and moon are like the spirit of night and day, their bodies.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r4.anchor: ولما كانت الظلمة عدما والنور وجودا والعدم مقدم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r5.claim: An unnamed poetic saying calls the created universe a message from the highest King to humanity and says everything besides God is vain.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r5.anchor: تأمل سطور الكائنات فإنها من الملك الأعلى إليك رسائل

BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r6.claim: The repeated negation stresses that each object is separately forbidden, and the moon is named explicitly instead of being left to a pronoun.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r6.anchor: أعاد النافي تأكيدا للنفي لأن النهي عن كل منهما على حدته

BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r7.claim: The sun is described as the greatest of the worshippers' idols, though it too is one of God's created things.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r7.anchor: التي هي أعظم أوثانكم فإنها من جملة مبدعاته

BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r8.claim: Only God, possessor of every perfection without defect, deserves prostration because He created the four signs; the feminine plural pronoun follows the convention for inanimate things and underscores their lowliness as deities.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r8.anchor: أي الأربعة لأجلكم فهو الذي يستحق الإلهية

BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r9.claim: He entertains another explanation for the feminine plural: the moon is counted as multiple moons because it changes through crescent, full, and dark phases.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r9.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون عد القمر أقمارا لأنه يكون تارة هلالا وأخرى بدرا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r10.claim: True worship must belong exclusively to God: prostrating even once to another makes the worship shirk, and God accepts only sincere worship because He is utterly self-sufficient.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r10.anchor: فإن أشركتم به شيئا بسجود أو غيره فما خصصتموه بالعبادة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r11.claim: Their claim that they worship idols only to bring them nearer to God (39:3) conflicts with their own exclusive invocations in distress, especially at sea.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r11.anchor: كما هو صريح قولكم في الدعاء في وقت الشدائد لا سيما في البحر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r12.claim: The verse urges people to preserve human dignity by never prostrating to a creature: angels were commanded to prostrate to Adam, while Iblīs refused, marking opposite stations.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p574/r12.anchor: أمر الملائكة الذين هم أشرف خلقه بعدهم بالسجود آدم وهم في ظهره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r1.claim: The paired prohibition and command imply exclusive worship: prostrate only to God, rather than to the sun or moon.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r1.anchor: فكأنه قيل : لا تسجدوا إلا لله ، أي دون الشمس والقمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r2.claim: The prohibition and command in verse 37 interrupt the connection between the signs of night and day and the conditional clause in verse 38.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r2.anchor: فجملة { لا تسجدوا للشمس } إلى قوله : { تعبدون } معترضة بين جملة { ومن ءاياته الليل والنهار }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r3.speaker: مالك وأصحابه عدا ابن وهب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r3.claim: Malik and his companions except Ibn Wahb place the prostration of recitation at the end of verse 37.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r3.anchor: فقال مالك وأصحابه عدا ابن وهب : السجود عند قوله تعالى : { إن كنتم إياه تعبدون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r4.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib and Ibn Masud are also reported to place the recitation prostration at the end of verse 37.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r4.anchor: وهو قول علي بن أبي طالب وابن مسعود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r5.speaker: الشافعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p300/r5.claim: A view placing the recitation prostration at the end of verse 37 is also reported from al-Shafiʿi.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r5.claim: Night and day invite reflection on changing lengths, overlap, and equality in different places; sun and moon display wonders, divine wisdom, and benefit to people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r5.anchor: وذكرهما يتضمن ما فيهما من القصر والطول والتداخل والاستواء في مواضع وسائر عبرهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r6.claim: Even useful celestial bodies should not be worshipped: their benefit comes from God’s subjection of them, so God alone deserves prostration.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r6.anchor: لا تسجدوا لهذه المخلوقات وإن كانت تنفعكم، لأن النفع منهما إنما هو بتسخير الله إياهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r7.claim: One group says the plural pronoun refers to the days mentioned earlier.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r7.anchor: قالت فرقة: هو عائد على الأيام المتقدم ذكرها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r8.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r8.claim: Another group takes the pronoun to refer to the sun and moon, treating a pair as a plural and non-rational plurals as feminine.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r8.anchor: وقالت فرقة: الضمير عائد على الشمس والقمر، والاثنان جمع، وجمع ما لا يعقل يؤنث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r9.claim: Because Arabic uses the plurals shumūs and aqmār for the celestial bodies, the collective plural agreement is possible for sun and moon.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r9.anchor: ومن حيث يقال شموس وأقمار لاختلافهما بالأيام، ساغ أن يعود الضمير مجموعا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r10.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r10.claim: A third group refers the pronoun to all four objects; non-rational plurals below ten may take this feminine plural agreement.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r10.anchor: وقالت فرقة: هو عائد على الأربعة المذكورة، وشأن ضمير ما لا يعقل إذا كان العدد أقل من العشرة أن يجيء هكذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r11.claim: The example from 9:36 shows feminine plural agreement with a non-rational plural.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16#3/r12.claim: Ibn Atiyya cites Hassan ibn Thabit’s line as another grammatical example of feminine plural agreement; its words continue in the next segment.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p182/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p182/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p182/r1.claim: Alternating night and day, the sun, and the moon’s changing course and phases let people measure days, months, and years and know when rights, worship, and transactions are due.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p182/r1.anchor: ويتبين بذلك حلول الحقوق، وأوقات العبادات والمعاملات.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p182/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p182/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p182/r2.claim: The sun and moon are among the finest visible bodies, yet are created servants under God’s power; worship belongs to God alone, since associating partners with Him is not forgiven.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p182/r2.anchor: أنهما مخلوقان عبدان من عبيده، تحت قهره وتسخيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p182/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p182/r4.speaker: جابر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p182/r4.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet forbade cursing night, day, sun, moon, and winds, since they may be sent as mercy to some people and punishment to others.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p182/r4.anchor: عن جابر (1) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تسبوا الليل ولا النهار

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r1.claim: Night and day are signs through their stable measure and ordered alternation, serving wisdom and benefit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r1.anchor: ووجه الآيات فيهما تقديرهما على حد مستقر , وتسييرهما على نظم مستمر , يتغايران لحكمة ويختلفان لمصلحة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r2.claim: The sun and moon are signs through distinctive light and the governance and measure displayed in them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r2.anchor: ووجه الآية فيهما ما خصهما به من نور , وأظهره فيهما من تدبير وتقدير .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r3.speaker: الزجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says “them” refers to the signs just mentioned.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج : أي خلق هذه الآيات .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r4.claim: Ibn Masud and al-Hasan place the prostration at the end of “if you worship Him.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r4.anchor: أحدهما : عند قوله { إن كنتم إياه تعبدون } قاله ابن مسعود والحسن .

MUQATIL:41:36-38/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:41:36-38/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:41:36-38/r4.claim: Created signs make God's oneness knowable through His workmanship even though He is unseen.
MUQATIL:41:36-38/r4.anchor: أن يعرف التوحيد بصنعه، وإن لم تروه

MUQATIL:41:36-38/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:41:36-38/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:41:36-38/r5.claim: The sun and moon are created signs, so worship belongs to their creator rather than to them.

MUQATIL:41:36-38/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:41:36-38/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:41:36-38/r6.claim: The Prophet and believers prostrated, prompting Meccan polytheists to say they would instead worship al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat.
MUQATIL:41:36-38/r6.anchor: فسجد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنون يومئذ، فقال كفار مكة عند ذلك: بل نسجد للات، والعزى، ومناة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r1.claim: Night and day point to oneness through their measured succession and alternation; sun and moon do so through their assigned courses and fixed light.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r1.anchor: في تعاقبهما على حد معلوم وتناوبهما على قدر مقسوم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r2.claim: The sun and moon are created beings, despite their many benefits, so they are not to be worshipped.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r3.claim: The feminine plural pronoun refers either to the signs or to the four non-rational entities; such plurals take feminine agreement, as in the examples about pens.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r3.anchor: الضمير في خلقهن للآيات أو الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر لان حكم جماعة ما لا يعقل حكم الانثى أو الاناث

NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r4.claim: Some people, like the star-worshipping Sabians, prostrated to sun and moon while claiming to intend Allah; the verse forbids this intermediary and demands worship directed purely to Allah.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r4.anchor: ولعل ناسا منهم كانوا يسجدون للشمس والقمر كالصابئين في عبادتهم الكواكب ويزعمون انهم يقصدون بالسجود لهما السجود لله تعالى فنهوا عن هذه الواسطة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r5.claim: If someone worships another alongside Allah, he is not truly worshipping Allah; the command requires exclusive monotheism.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#2/r5.anchor: وامروا ان يقصدوا بسجودهم وجه الله خالصا ان كانوا اياه يعبدون وكانوا موحدين غير مشركين فان من عبد مع الله غيره لا يكون عابدا لله

QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r1.claim: Night, day, sun, and moon are signs pointing to God's oneness and power.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r2.claim: The celestial bodies do not deserve worship by their own virtue; God created them and could erase or extinguish them.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r2.anchor: فليس ذلك لفضيلة لهما في أنفسهما فيستحقان بها العبادة

QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r3.claim: The pronoun in khalaqahunna returns to sun, moon, night, and day.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r3.anchor: فالكناية ترجع إلى الشمس والقمر والليل والنهار

QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r4.claim: An alternative takes the pronoun as referring only to the sun and moon, with a dual referred to in plural form.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r4.anchor: وقيل: للشمس والقمر خاصة لأن الاثنين جمع

QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r5.claim: Another alternative makes the pronoun refer to the meaning of āyāt, signs.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r5.anchor: وقيل: الضمير عائد على معنى الآيات

QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r6.claim: The feminine plural follows a plural of non-rational beings rather than applying masculine-feminine prevalence.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r6.anchor: وإنما أنث على جمع التكثير ولم يجر على طريق التغليب

QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r7.claim: If they worship God, they should prostrate to Him alone, the one who created, formed, and subjected these signs.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r7.anchor: واسجدوا لله الذي خلقهن } وصورهن وسخرهن

QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r10.claim: There is consensus that the passage is a prostration verse, though authorities disagree about exactly where to prostrate.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r10.anchor: هذه الآية آية سجدة بلا خلاف واختلفوا في موضع السجود

QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r11.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r11.claim: Malik places the prostration at 'if you worship Him,' because it is connected to the command; Ali, Ibn Masʿud, and others did likewise.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r11.anchor: فقال مالك: موضعه { إن كنتم إياه تعبدون } لأنه متصل بالأمر

QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r16.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r16.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the disagreement about the prostration point is a minor matter.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r17.speaker: ابن خويزمنداد
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r17.claim: Ibn Khuwayz Mandad says the verse includes lunar and solar eclipse prayer because Arabs associated eclipses with the death of a great person, prompting the Prophet's prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r17.anchor: ذكر ابن خويزمنداد: أن هذه الآية تضمنت صلاة كسوف القمر والشمس

QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r18.claim: Al-Qurtubi confirms eclipse prayer in al-Bukhari and Muslim; its forms vary with reports, and Sahih Muslim is the authority on the subject.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r18.anchor: قلت: صلاة الكسوف ثابتة في الصحاح البخاري ومسلم وغيرهما
